trust_decision.summary: ADVISORY/FIX MISMATCH. The advisory (code-node RCE, CWE-95/1392/306/653/863) is already closed at the pinned commit: the local in-process executor is disabled. The only diff with content (189600dd, PR #1669) is an SSRF fix: it decides whether a caller-supplied outbound URL (tool endpoint, image/OCR file URL) may be fetched. That decision is in console UrlCheckTool.checkUrl/checkBlackList (Java), in core-link HttpRun (tool executor) and in core-aitools download helpers.

landing_point.why: For the SSRF diff, a report about outbound plugin requests leads to the core-link HttpRun executor, which makes the actual request with a default aiohttp session. For the advisory as titled (code node), the landing point would be core/workflow/engine/nodes/code/executor/local/local_executor.py:17, and that is already fixed.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /create-tool (ToolBoxController.java:29-39): validates stored entity endpoint instead of submitted DTO endpoint
UrlCheckTool.checkUrl via create-tool/update-tool/debug-tool (ToolBoxService.java:176,354,536); the validator itself issues a HEAD probe to the user URL (redirect follow)
same checkUrl callers; domain whitelist returns before restricted-address check
core-link http_run / tool_debug (core/plugin/link/service/community/tools/http/execution_server.py:723,746) - urljoin path param can replace origin
core-link http_run / tool_debug - no connection-bound IP check (DNS-resolved private targets pass)
HttpRun.__init__ blacklist (literal-IP only, fail-open on exception at process.py:84-87)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: core/plugin/aitools/service/ocr_llm/req_ase_ability_ocr_service.py:525 and core/plugin/aitools/service/image_understanding/image_understanding_service.py:33 (separate service, separate package from core-link/console; fix adds a new safe_download module fix.diff:573-926)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The aitools OCR and image-understanding downloads are 'file input' features in a different microservice, not 'outbound plugin requests', so a solver focused on tool endpoints can argue they are a neighbouring feature. For the MCP route (O8): MCP is a different transport/protocol (SSE) with its own blacklist and local-URL check.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Trusted official internal tools and configured private endpoints must keep working: debug of seeded official tools skips checkUrl (ToolBoxService.java:535-537), and core-link must still reach core-aitools internal endpoints (fix adds PRIVATE_ENDPOINT_ALLOW_LIST, fix.diff:1506-1510). The aitools fetch must still accept the configured private MinIO/S3 bucket origin (fix.diff:846-886). IP-literal whitelist entries must still pass (UrlCheckTool.java:256-259).

O6_input_shapes: literal private/loopback/link-local IPv4 and IPv6 host
IPv4-mapped IPv6 and NAT64/6to4 IPv6 forms (fix.diff:609-628, 912-926)
hostname that resolves (or rebinds) to a private address - checked at socket connect (fix.diff:635-655, 2024-2047)
redirect to a private target (validator HEAD probe removed; requests made with allow_redirects=False)
path parameter that is absolute, scheme-relative or a dot segment and replaces the origin via urljoin (fix.diff:1649-1678)
userinfo, backslash in authority, fragment, control characters (fix.diff:775-803)
domain-whitelisted host resolving to a restricted address (fix.diff:180-199)
create-tool with a new endpoint on a fresh entity (DTO vs entity, fix.diff:13-20)

O7_producer.where: console/backend/toolkit/src/main/java/com/iflytek/astron/console/toolkit/service/tool/ToolBoxService.java:175-179 (check reads toolBox entity before buildToolBox copies the DTO endpoint into it)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: core-link MCP tool-list by URL and MCP call-tool use the old access_interceptor.is_in_blacklist (literal configured IP/CIDR plus substring domain match) and a loopback-only is_local_url; there is no DNS/connect-time private-address check and the fix leaves both unchanged
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: MCP is a separate transport (SSE/streamable) with its own error codes; the advisory is about HTTP plugin tool calls
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same core-link package; different module (utils/security/access_interceptor.py vs infra/tool_exector/ssrf_guard.py)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MCP call-tool: caller-supplied mcp_server_url checked only by is_in_blacklist before the connection
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above; the URL may also come from the DB (get_mcp_server_url), so it looks like 'stored config'

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Shared old blacklist helper that a code comment says is duplicated across access_interceptor.py and tool_exector/process.py; the fix replaced only the process.py copy
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Looks like a general utility rather than the tool-call path

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an image-generate variant that fetches a caller-supplied reference image URL via HttpClient
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Sibling aitools services already fetch caller URLs with the same HttpClient (ocr :525, image_understanding :33)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the MCP SSE connect with no connection-bound address check (mirrors the old HttpRun)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The MCP transport opens its own client outside HttpRun, so a maintainer porting the guard to HttpRun would plausibly miss it

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918) in the fix diff; the advisory claims code injection/unsandboxed execution (CWE-95), but that is already fixed at the pinned commit

O10_build.toolchain: Maven for console/backend; uv/pytest for core/plugin/link and core/plugin/aitools
services: none needed for the Python unit tests
